intent.raw_query: Thailand beaches, $1800 for couple, mix of island hopping and street food, October 2026

selected_hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Phi Phi Islands Snorkeling & Island Hopping Tour
experiences.description: Embark on a full-day speedboat tour hopping between the stunning Phi Phi islands, including Maya Bay (made famous by The Beach), Monkey Beach, and Pileh Lagoon. Snorkel in crystal-clear turquoise waters teeming with colorful marine life and enjoy breathtaking limestone karst scenery.

experiences.name: Bangkok Street Food Night Walk in Yaowarat
experiences.description: Dive into Bangkok's legendary street food scene in Chinatown's Yaowarat Road. Sample iconic dishes like pad thai, mango sticky rice, grilled satay, boat noodles, and fresh seafood from bustling roadside stalls and hawker carts. Join a guided food tour or explore independently through the vibrant night market atmosphere.

experiences.name: Koh Lanta & Koh Rok Island Hopping by Longtail Boat
experiences.description: Explore the laid-back paradise of Koh Lanta and take a day trip to the remote Koh Rok islands, known for their pristine white sand beaches, vibrant coral reefs, and incredibly clear emerald waters. Ideal for snorkeling, swimming, and escaping the crowds in a more untouched tropical setting.

experiences.name: Chiang Mai Street Food & Night Bazaar Experience
experiences.description: Wander through Chiang Mai's famous Night Bazaar and Sunday Walking Street, sampling authentic Northern Thai street food including khao soi (coconut curry noodle soup), sai oua (Northern Thai sausage), and crispy pork rinds. Immerse yourself in the cultural blend of local crafts, live music, and traditional flavors unique to Northern Thailand.

experiences.name: Koh Samui Beach Hopping & Ang Thong Marine Park Tour
experiences.description: Join a full-day boat excursion to the stunning Ang Thong National Marine Park, an archipelago of 42 islands with dramatic limestone formations, hidden lagoons, and pristine beaches. Kayak through sea caves, hike to a panoramic viewpoint, and snorkel in the emerald green saltwater lake — one of Thailand's most spectacular natural wonders.
experiences.location: Ang Thong National Marine Park, Koh Samui, Surat Thani

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Thailand
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Suvarnabhumi or Phuket Airport at 13:00. Clear customs, exchange currency at an airport booth for decent rates, and grab a local SIM card (AIS or DTAC, ~150 THB). Take a budget minivan or shared shuttle to the pier (Rassada Pier in Phuket or Ao Nang in Krabi). Board the ferry to Phi Phi Islands (approx. 90–120 THB). Check in to your boutique stay on Phi Phi Don and freshen up.
day_by_day.evening: Take a relaxed stroll along Tonsai Bay waterfront. Explore the lively walking street and get your bearings on the island. Watch the sunset from the beachfront promenade.

meals.breakfast: Grab a snack or light meal at the airport — look for 7-Eleven or airport food court (~80–120 THB)
meals.lunch: Quick bite at pier food stalls before boarding the ferry — pad kra pao or fried rice (~60–80 THB)
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local Thai restaurant on Tonsai walking street — try massaman curry with rice (~100–150 THB). Avoid tourist-facing menus and look for spots filled with locals.

day_by_day.notes: Keep arrival day light. Hydrate well after travel. Confirm ferry schedules in advance as they may vary by season. October is shoulder/low season — expect occasional rain but fewer crowds and lower prices.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and hike up to the Phi Phi Viewpoint (free entry, roughly 20–30 min climb). The panoramic view of the twin bays is stunning and best enjoyed before the midday heat. Bring water and wear good shoes.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Loh Dalum Bay for a swim and beach relaxation. Rent a snorkel set from a local shop (~100 THB/hour) and explore the shallow reef near the bay. Alternatively, join a budget longtail boat trip to nearby Monkey Beach (~200–300 THB shared).
day_by_day.evening: Join a fire show on the beach at Tonsai Bay — many bars host these for free nightly. Grab a cheap bucket cocktail (~150 THB) and enjoy the entertainment.

meals.breakfast: Banana pancake from a street stall near the pier (~40–60 THB) with fresh fruit shake
meals.lunch: Pad Thai or spring rolls from a beachside food shack on Loh Dalum Bay (~80–100 THB)
meals.dinner: Street food dinner on Tonsai walking street — grilled satay skewers, mango sticky rice, and som tum (~150 THB total)

day_by_day.notes: Viewpoint hike is best before 9:00 AM to beat the heat and crowds. Wear reef-safe sunscreen to protect the coral ecosystem.

day_by_day.morning: Book a shared snorkeling day trip to Phi Phi Leh — the island made famous by The Beach film. Visit Maya Bay (entry fee ~400 THB), Pileh Lagoon, and Viking Cave. Shared boat tours typically depart at 8:00–9:00 AM (~600–900 THB per person including snorkel gear).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the island-hopping tour. Snorkel at Hin Klang reef and look for reef sharks, clownfish, and sea turtles. Return to Phi Phi Don by early afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Relax and recover from the day on the beach. Visit a local massage parlor for a traditional Thai massage (~200–250 THB for 1 hour).

meals.breakfast: Toast and eggs at a small guesthouse café near the pier (~80 THB)
meals.lunch: Packed lunch often included in boat tour, or buy snacks from a floating vendor near Maya Bay
meals.dinner: Fresh seafood BBQ on the beach — many stalls offer grilled fish, prawns, and squid by weight (~200–300 THB). Look for stalls away from the main tourist drag for better prices.

day_by_day.notes: Maya Bay has restricted visitor numbers and timed entry slots — book your tour the evening before to secure a spot. Bring biodegradable sunscreen only.

day_by_day.morning: Take the morning ferry from Phi Phi Don to Ao Nang, Krabi (~150–200 THB, about 90 min). Check in to a budget guesthouse in Ao Nang or Krabi Town. Drop bags and head out to explore Ao Nang Beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a kayak at Ao Nang Beach (~200–300 THB/hour) and paddle around the limestone karsts. Alternatively, take a longtail boat to Railay Beach (~100 THB one way) — a stunning beach only accessible by boat.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Ao Nang's night market and street food scene. Walk the main strip and sample various dishes from different vendors.

meals.breakfast: Grab breakfast on Phi Phi before the ferry — roti with banana and condensed milk (~40 THB)
meals.lunch: Beachside restaurant at Railay or Ao Nang — green curry with jasmine rice (~100–130 THB)
meals.dinner: Ao Nang night market — try grilled corn, fried noodles, and mango shake (~100–150 THB total)

day_by_day.notes: Ferry from Phi Phi to Ao Nang typically departs at 9:00 AM and 1:00 PM — book the morning ferry. Railay Beach is worth the short longtail ride; it's one of Thailand's most scenic spots.

day_by_day.morning: Take a half-day 4-island boat tour from Ao Nang Pier — visits Chicken Island, Tup Island, Poda Island, and Mor Island (~600–800 THB shared, includes snorkeling). Departs around 8:30 AM.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return by early afternoon. Visit the Tiger Cave Temple (Wat Tham Suea) — a revered Buddhist temple with 1,237 steps to the summit offering panoramic views of Krabi. Entry is free. Take a songthaew (red shared taxi) from Ao Nang to Krabi Town (~50 THB).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Krabi Town's lively night market — Chao Fa Night Market runs Thursday to Sunday and is excellent for street food and local crafts.

meals.breakfast: Toast with peanut butter and coffee at a small café (~60–80 THB)
meals.lunch: Snacks and fresh coconut on the island tour, or eat at the pier food stalls on return (~80–100 THB)
meals.dinner: Krabi Town night market — try khao man gai (poached chicken rice), grilled seafood, and fresh fruit (~150–200 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Tiger Cave Temple requires modest dress — cover shoulders and knees. The climb is strenuous but rewarding; go in the late afternoon to avoid peak heat. Bring plenty of water.

day_by_day.morning: Take a half-day kayaking tour through the mangroves and sea caves of Ao Thalane or Bor Thor (~400–600 THB for a guided group tour). This is a unique eco-experience through hidden lagoons and limestone caves.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to Ao Nang and spend the afternoon at Nopparat Thara Beach — a quieter, less commercialized beach just 2 km from Ao Nang (free entry). Swim, relax, and enjoy the scenery.
day_by_day.evening: Head back to Ao Nang for dinner and a casual evening. Browse the souvenir shops along the main strip for budget gifts.

meals.breakfast: Local Thai breakfast of jok (rice porridge) with egg from a street stall (~50 THB)
meals.lunch: Beachside restaurant near Nopparat Thara — pad see ew or fried rice (~90–120 THB)
meals.dinner: Restaurant on Ao Nang main street — tom yum soup and stir-fried vegetables with rice (~150 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Nopparat Thara Beach is accessible by songthaew or bicycle rental (~50–80 THB/day). October may bring some afternoon rain — keep a light rain jacket handy.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take a bus or minivan from Krabi to Koh Lanta (~150–200 THB, about 2 hours including a short ferry crossing). Check in to a budget bungalow on Long Beach (Hat Khlong Dao) or Klong Nin Beach.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a scooter (~200–250 THB/day) and explore the island at your own pace. Visit Koh Lanta Old Town on the east coast — a charming fishing village with wooden stilt houses, local cafés, and a relaxed atmosphere.
day_by_day.evening: Watch the sunset from the west coast beach — Klong Nin or Long Beach offer spectacular views. Many beach bars have bean bag chairs right on the sand.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departure in Ao Nang — noodle soup from a street vendor (~50–60 THB)
meals.lunch: Old Town café in Koh Lanta — fresh seafood or Thai curry (~120–150 THB)
meals.dinner: Beachfront restaurant on Long Beach — BBQ fish with sticky rice and papaya salad (~180–220 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Koh Lanta is more relaxed and less crowded than Phi Phi, making it great for a slower pace. Scooter rental requires a valid license — ride carefully on island roads. Fuel up at local petrol stations (small bottles sold roadside).

day_by_day.morning: Visit Koh Lanta Marine National Park at the southern tip of the island (entry fee ~200 THB). Explore the lighthouse, mangrove boardwalk, and pristine beaches. Arrive early to beat any crowds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Snorkel at the park's coral reef — rent gear from the park entrance (~100 THB). The reef here is less damaged than in busier areas. Alternatively, take a longtail to nearby Koh Rok (~800–1000 THB shared day trip) for world-class snorkeling.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your beach area. Enjoy a slow evening — grab street food from a night market stall or cook-your-own BBQ setup at a local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Fruit bowl and yogurt from a health café near Long Beach (~80–100 THB)
meals.lunch: Pack snacks or eat at the national park food stall — simple rice and curry (~80 THB)
meals.dinner: Local Thai restaurant away from the beach strip — ask your guesthouse for a recommendation (~120–150 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Koh Rok day trip is one of the best snorkeling experiences in Thailand — highly recommended if budget allows. Book through your guesthouse for the best group rates.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a bicycle (~100 THB/day) or scooter and explore the quieter northern beaches of Koh Lanta — visit Khlong Dao Beach and Phra Ae (Long Beach) for a morning swim. Stop at a local bakery for a slow breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Tham Khao Mai Kaew caves in the island's interior (~200 THB with guide). Explore the stalactite-filled caverns and natural rock pools. The guided tour is essential for safety and takes about 1–2 hours.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Klong Nin Beach for the famous Koh Lanta sunset. Many small beach bars and restaurants line this stretch — enjoy a cold Chang beer (~60 THB) while watching the sky turn orange.

meals.breakfast: Pastry and coffee at a local bakery near Long Beach (~80–100 THB)
meals.lunch: Street food near the cave area — grilled corn, fried tofu, and fresh coconut (~80 THB)
meals.dinner: Seafood dinner at Klong Nin Beach — grilled barracuda or red snapper with garlic and chili (~200–250 THB)

day_by_day.notes: The cave tour involves some crawling and swimming — wear clothes you don't mind getting wet. Bring a dry bag for your phone and valuables.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day: Take a ferry or speedboat from Koh Lanta to Koh Ngai or back to Krabi, then connect to Koh Jum — a quieter, less-developed island great for budget travelers (~300–400 THB total). Check in to a simple beach bungalow.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Koh Jum on foot or by rented bicycle. The island has no ATMs, so bring enough cash. Visit the local fishing village and interact with the friendly Muslim fishing community.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy a quiet evening on the beach — Koh Jum is famous for its dark skies and stargazing. Bring a flashlight as the island has limited street lighting.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departure on Koh Lanta — roti with egg (~50 THB)
meals.lunch: Simple Thai lunch at a local family restaurant on Koh Jum (~80–100 THB)
meals.dinner: Beachside restaurant on Koh Jum — fresh catch of the day grilled with herbs (~150–180 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Koh Jum is ideal for travelers wanting to escape crowds. Bring cash, insect repellent, and a good book. Mobile signal is limited — enjoy the digital detox. Confirm ferry connections the evening before.

day_by_day.morning: Spend a slow morning on Koh Jum's deserted beaches — walk south along the shoreline and find your own private stretch of sand. Swim in calm, clear water.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the afternoon ferry back to the mainland (Laem Kruat pier) and connect to Krabi Town by songthaew (~50 THB). Check in to a budget guesthouse in Krabi Town for the night. Visit the Chao Fa Pier walking street.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Krabi Town's food scene — this is where locals eat and prices are the lowest of the trip. Visit the weekend walking street or riverside restaurants.

meals.breakfast: Fresh tropical fruit platter at your bungalow (~60 THB)
meals.lunch: Pack snacks from a local shop for the ferry ride (~50 THB)
meals.dinner: Krabi Town local restaurant — khao soi (northern curry noodle soup) or boat noodles (~80–100 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Krabi Town is often overlooked by tourists but offers excellent authentic food and a glimpse into real Thai daily life. The riverside area is particularly charming in the evening.

day_by_day.morning: Take a day trip to the Emerald Pool (Sa Morakot) and Blue Pool in Khao Phra Bang Khram Nature Reserve (~200 THB entry). These natural mineral pools in the jungle are stunning. Arrive early — by 8:00 AM — before tour groups arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the nearby Hot Springs Waterfall (~90 THB entry) — natural hot spring water cascades into a stream where you can soak your feet and relax in the warm pools. A truly unique experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Krabi Town. Spend your last evening doing some final souvenir shopping and eating your favorite Thai dishes one more time. Pack your bags for departure.

meals.breakfast: Rice soup with pork from a local morning market stall in Krabi Town (~50 THB)
meals.lunch: Picnic snacks near the Emerald Pool — buy from the entrance food stalls (~80–100 THB)
meals.dinner: Farewell Thai feast at a riverside restaurant in Krabi — order a spread of tom yum, pad thai, and green curry to share (~200–250 THB)

day_by_day.notes: Rent a scooter or join a shared minivan tour to reach the Emerald Pool (~300–400 THB for shared transport). The Blue Pool has limited visitor access — check current rules on arrival. Wear water shoes if possible.

day_by_day.morning: Enjoy a final leisurely Thai breakfast in Krabi Town. Do any last-minute shopping at the morning market. Head to Krabi Airport by songthaew or taxi (~150–200 THB) in time for your departure flight. Check in and clear security.
day_by_day.afternoon: Departure. Reflect on 13 incredible days of island hopping, street food adventures, and beach bliss across Thailand's southern coast.
day_by_day.evening: In-flight or onward travel.

meals.breakfast: Final Thai breakfast — khao tom (rice soup) or fried eggs with toast at a local café (~60–80 THB)
meals.lunch: Airport food court or grab snacks for the flight (~100–150 THB)
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or at connecting airport

day_by_day.notes: Krabi Airport (KBV) is small — arrive at least 2 hours before departure. If flying via Bangkok, allow extra time for connections. Keep some Thai Baht for airport food and last-minute expenses. Declare any food items at customs on return.

trip_options.title: Classic Thailand Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and prepare for transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: After landing, clear customs and take a pre-arranged ferry or speedboat transfer from Krabi or Phuket pier to Phi Phi Islands (approx. 1.5–2 hours). Check into your boutique stay, freshen up, and take a relaxed stroll along Tonsai Bay to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the lively Tonsai Village night scene. Browse the beachfront walking street, enjoy the warm sea breeze, and settle in for a welcome dinner at a local restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the airport before or during your flight — grab a snack or light meal at Krabi/Phuket airport cafes.
meals.lunch: Quick bite at the pier before boarding the ferry — try a simple Thai noodle soup or pad thai from a pier-side stall (~150–200 THB).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Papaya Restaurant on Tonsai Bay — fresh seafood, green curry, and mango sticky rice. Mid-range meal (~300–450 THB per person).

day_by_day.notes: Book your ferry transfer in advance. October can bring some rain — pack a light rain jacket. Keep your first evening low-key to recover from travel.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and hike up to the Phi Phi Viewpoint (30–45 min hike). Catch a stunning panoramic view of both Tonsai and Loh Dalum bays before the heat sets in. Return to your hotel for a relaxed breakfast.
day_by_day.afternoon: Join a half-day snorkeling longtail boat tour around Phi Phi Don — visit Monkey Beach, Viking Cave, and the crystal-clear waters of Pileh Lagoon. Most tours run 1–4 PM (~600–900 THB per person).
day_by_day.evening: Return to the village and explore the street food stalls along the main walking street. Watch fire shows on Loh Dalum Beach — a nightly Phi Phi tradition.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your boutique hotel or a nearby café — toast, eggs, fresh fruit, and Thai iced coffee (~150–200 THB).
meals.lunch: Pack snacks for the boat tour or grab a quick lunch before departure — coconut pancakes or spring rolls from a street stall (~80–120 THB).
meals.dinner: Street food dinner on Tonsai walking street — grilled satay skewers, pad see ew, fresh fruit shakes, and mango with sticky rice (~200–300 THB total).

day_by_day.notes: Bring reef-safe sunscreen, a dry bag, and water shoes for the snorkeling tour. Negotiate longtail boat prices or book through your hotel for better rates.

day_by_day.morning: Early morning kayaking around the quieter east coast of Phi Phi Don — paddle through mangroves and hidden coves before the crowds arrive. Rent kayaks from the beach (~200–300 THB/hour).
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a speedboat day trip to the iconic Maya Bay on Phi Phi Leh (made famous by 'The Beach'). Swim in the turquoise waters, explore the surrounding cliffs, and snorkel at nearby Loh Samah Bay. Tours depart around noon (~800–1,200 THB).
day_by_day.evening: Sunset drinks at a beachfront bar on Loh Dalum Beach. Watch the sky turn golden over the bay before heading to dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a local café near Tonsai pier — banana pancakes, fresh fruit bowl, and iced tea (~150–180 THB).
meals.lunch: Pack lunch from a street stall to eat on the boat, or enjoy a beachside snack at Maya Bay (~100–150 THB).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Unni's Restaurant, Phi Phi — popular mid-range spot with excellent Thai curries and seafood (~350–500 THB per person).

day_by_day.notes: Maya Bay has regulated visitor hours and capacity limits — book your tour early. October weather may cause occasional afternoon showers; tours usually proceed unless there are strong winds.

day_by_day.morning: Relax morning on Loh Dalum Beach — swim, sunbathe, or take a yoga class offered by several beachfront studios. Enjoy the calm before the day-trippers arrive.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a longtail boat to the quieter Loh Moo Dee Bay or Rantee Beach on the east side of Phi Phi Don for a more secluded beach experience. Bring a book, snorkel, and plenty of water.
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Phi Phi local market near the village center for fresh produce, handmade crafts, and local snacks. Great for souvenirs and people-watching.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your hotel — enjoy a full Thai breakfast with rice porridge (jok), fried egg, and fresh juice (~150–200 THB).
meals.lunch: Beachside lunch at a small shack near Rantee Beach — grilled fish, papaya salad, and coconut water (~200–280 THB).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Cosmic Restaurant, Phi Phi — laid-back atmosphere, great Thai-Western fusion menu, and affordable prices (~300–400 THB per person).

day_by_day.notes: This is a lighter, more relaxed day — ideal for recharging mid-trip. Stay hydrated and apply sunscreen regularly, especially in October humidity.

day_by_day.morning: Check out of your Phi Phi boutique stay. Take the morning ferry to Krabi Town (approx. 1.5 hours). Check into a mid-range guesthouse or hotel in Krabi Town and drop off your bags.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Wat Tham Seua (Tiger Cave Temple) — climb 1,237 steps to the summit for a breathtaking 360° view of Krabi's karst landscape and surrounding jungle. (~30 THB entry).
day_by_day.evening: Explore Krabi Town's famous Walking Street Night Market (open Thursday–Sunday; if not available, visit the Chao Fa Night Market instead). Sample local street food, browse handicrafts, and soak up the local atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast near Tonsai pier before departure — roti with banana and condensed milk, Thai iced coffee (~100–150 THB).
meals.lunch: Lunch in Krabi Town after arrival — try a local restaurant near the waterfront for khao man gai (poached chicken rice) or tom yum soup (~120–180 THB).
meals.dinner: Night market dinner in Krabi Town — grilled meats, pad thai, som tam, fresh coconut ice cream, and local sweets (~200–300 THB for a full spread).

day_by_day.notes: The Tiger Cave Temple climb is strenuous — wear comfortable shoes and go in the late afternoon to avoid peak heat. Bring water. Confirm night market schedule based on the day of the week.

day_by_day.morning: Join a Four Islands boat tour departing from Krabi Town or Ao Nang — visit Koh Mor, Koh Chueak, Koh Tub, and Koh Chicken. Snorkel, swim, and walk the famous sandbar connecting two islands at low tide (~600–900 THB).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the island-hopping tour through the afternoon. Return to the mainland by late afternoon and take a tuk-tuk or songthaew to Ao Nang Beach for a stroll.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Ao Nang's beachfront strip — lively but more relaxed than Phuket. Browse shops, enjoy a beachside cocktail, and watch the longtail boats lit up in the bay at dusk.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Krabi hotel or a nearby café — eggs, toast, fresh fruit (~150 THB).
meals.lunch: Lunch included with most Four Islands tours — typically a simple Thai buffet on a beach or boat (~included or ~150 THB extra).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Last Fisherman Bar & Restaurant, Ao Nang — fresh seafood, great views, mid-range prices (~350–500 THB per person).

day_by_day.notes: Book the Four Islands tour the evening before. October tides affect the sandbar visibility — check timing with your tour operator.

day_by_day.morning: Take a longtail boat from Ao Nang to Railay Beach (15 minutes, ~100 THB each way) — accessible only by boat. Explore Railay West Beach and Railay East Beach in the morning while it's quieter.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike through the jungle to Phra Nang Cave and the stunning Phra Nang Beach — one of Thailand's most beautiful beaches, surrounded by dramatic limestone cliffs. Swim, relax, or try rock climbing with a local guide (~600–900 THB for a half-day intro session).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Ao Nang by longtail boat before sunset. Enjoy a relaxed evening with a Thai massage on the beach (~300–400 THB/hour) and a quiet dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a café in Ao Nang before heading to the pier — fresh fruit smoothie, toast with jam, soft-boiled eggs (~150–180 THB).
meals.lunch: Lunch at a beach restaurant on Railay West — grilled fish, green papaya salad, and fresh coconut (~250–350 THB).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Sala Thai Restaurant, Ao Nang — authentic Thai cuisine, generous portions, excellent value (~280–400 THB per person).

day_by_day.notes: Railay is a must-visit highlight. Arrive early to beat the crowds. Wear water shoes as the longtail boat landing can be wet. Keep valuables in a dry bag.

day_by_day.morning: Morning at leisure in Ao Nang or Krabi Town. Visit the Krabi Town waterfront and take a scenic long-tail boat ride along the mangrove-lined Krabi River (~200–300 THB for a private tour).
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel from Krabi to Koh Lanta by ferry (approx. 1.5–2 hours, ~350–500 THB). Check into a mid-range beachfront bungalow or guesthouse on Long Beach (Hat Khlong Dao). Relax on the wide, quiet beach.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Koh Lanta Old Town (Ban Si Raya) — a charming sea-gypsy village with wooden shophouses on stilts over the water. Browse local crafts and enjoy the sunset from the pier.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Krabi hotel or a local bakery — croissant, fresh juice, and yogurt with granola (~150–200 THB).
meals.lunch: Quick lunch at Krabi pier before the ferry — noodle soup or fried rice from a pier-side stall (~100–150 THB).
meals.dinner: Dinner at a beachfront restaurant in Koh Lanta Old Town — fresh grilled squid, massaman curry, and sticky rice (~300–400 THB per person).

day_by_day.notes: Ferry schedules from Krabi to Koh Lanta vary by season — book in advance. October is shoulder season; some services may be reduced. Confirm the day before.

day_by_day.morning: Rent a scooter or bicycle and explore Koh Lanta at your own pace. Head south along the coast road, stopping at Klong Nin Beach and Kantiang Bay — two of the island's most beautiful and secluded spots.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Mu Ko Lanta National Park at the southern tip of the island — jungle trails, a lighthouse with panoramic views, and a small beach. Entry fee ~200 THB. Swim at the park beach if conditions allow.
day_by_day.evening: Return north and catch the sunset from Sunset Point near Kantiang Bay or Long Beach. Enjoy a beachside bonfire (some resorts offer this) and a relaxed dinner.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your guesthouse or a nearby café — Thai omelette with rice, fresh fruit, and iced coffee (~150 THB).
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local restaurant near Kantiang Bay — pad thai, spring rolls, and fresh coconut water (~180–250 THB).
meals.dinner: Dinner at Drunken Sailors Bar & Restaurant, Koh Lanta — popular expat-friendly spot with great Thai and Western food, live music some nights (~300–450 THB per person).

day_by_day.notes: Scooter rental costs ~200–300 THB/day. Drive carefully — roads in the south can be steep and winding. Always wear a helmet. Fuel up before heading south.

day_by_day.morning: Join a full-day snorkeling and island-hopping tour from Koh Lanta to the Trang Islands — visit Koh Rok Nok and Koh Rok Nai, known for their pristine coral reefs, turquoise waters, and white sand beaches (~1,200–1,800 THB).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the tour with stops at Koh Chueak or Koh Waen for more snorkeling. These lesser-visited islands offer excellent marine life and fewer crowds than Phi Phi.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Koh Lanta by late afternoon. Enjoy a slow evening — Thai massage, sunset cocktails on the beach, and stargazing from the shore.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast before the tour departs — rice porridge or toast with eggs at your guesthouse (~120–150 THB).
meals.lunch: Lunch included with the tour — typically a beach BBQ or Thai lunch box on one of the islands.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Time for Lime Cooking School & Restaurant, Koh Lanta — excellent Thai food in a beautiful garden setting (~350–500 THB per person).

day_by_day.notes: The Trang Islands are a highlight — book this tour as early as possible. October seas can be choppy; check conditions with the operator the morning of the tour.

day_by_day.morning: Relaxed morning on Long Beach — swim, read, or take an optional cooking class at Time for Lime (~1,500–2,000 THB, includes market visit and 3-course meal). A fun and educational experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel back from Koh Lanta to Krabi by ferry, then onward to Phuket by minivan or bus (total travel time ~3–4 hours). Check into a mid-range hotel in Patong or Kata Beach area.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Phuket's famous Bangla Road in Patong for a lively evening — street performers, night markets, and vibrant nightlife. Keep it casual and enjoy the energy without overspending.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your Koh Lanta guesthouse — last morning treat of fresh fruit, pancakes, and coffee (~150–200 THB).
meals.lunch: Lunch during transit — grab food at Krabi bus terminal or a roadside restaurant (~150–200 THB).
meals.dinner: Dinner at a local restaurant near Patong Beach — try a seafood BBQ platter or massaman lamb curry at a mid-range restaurant (~350–500 THB per person).

day_by_day.notes: Book your Koh Lanta to Phuket transfer in advance — joint ferry+minivan tickets are available and convenient. Arrive in Phuket before dark if possible.

day_by_day.morning: Visit Phuket Old Town in the morning — explore the beautifully preserved Sino-Portuguese architecture, colorful street murals, and boutique coffee shops along Thalang Road and Soi Romanee.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Kata Beach or Karon Beach for a relaxed afternoon — these are calmer and more family-friendly than Patong. Swim, rent a beach chair, or try stand-up paddleboarding (~300–400 THB/hour).
day_by_day.evening: Visit the Phuket Weekend Night Market (Naka Market) if visiting on a weekend, or the Malin Plaza Night Market near Patong. Enjoy a final evening of street food, live music, and souvenir shopping.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a charming café in Phuket Old Town — try Kopitiam by Wilai for authentic Phuket-style breakfast with dim sum and local coffee (~180–250 THB).
meals.lunch: Lunch at a beachside restaurant in Kata — fresh fish, som tam, and cold Chang beer (~300–400 THB).
meals.dinner: Street food feast at the night market — grilled pork skewers, oyster omelette, mango sticky rice, fresh coconut, and Thai iced tea (~200–300 THB for a full spread).

day_by_day.notes: Phuket Old Town is best explored on foot in the morning before it gets too hot. Tuk-tuks in Phuket are expensive — negotiate fares or use Grab app for fair pricing.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Thailand — wake up early for a peaceful sunrise walk on the beach. Pack your bags and enjoy a leisurely last breakfast. Pick up any last-minute souvenirs from a local shop or market.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of your hotel and transfer to Phuket International Airport. Allow at least 2–3 hours before your flight for check-in and security. Reflect on 13 incredible days of beaches, islands, and street food.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Phuket International Airport. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Final Thai breakfast — go all out with a full spread at a local café: pad kra pao (basil stir-fry with fried egg on rice), fresh juice, and Thai iced coffee (~180–250 THB).
meals.lunch: Light lunch at the airport or near the hotel before departure — noodle soup or fried rice (~150–200 THB).
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or airport dining depending on departure time.

day_by_day.notes: Use Grab app for a reliable and fairly priced airport transfer. Phuket airport is about 30–45 minutes from Patong/Kata. Keep some Thai Baht for last-minute purchases or tips. Departure tax is included in most international tickets.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Thailand Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Phi Phi Islands, Krabi Province Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and prepare for transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private airport transfer to pier, then board a luxury speedboat charter to Phi Phi Islands. Check in to your boutique stay, unwind on the private terrace, and take a sunset stroll along Loh Dalum Bay beach.
day_by_day.evening: Welcome dinner at a beachfront restaurant on Phi Phi Don. Enjoy fresh grilled seafood platters, Thai-style lobster, and tropical cocktails with torchlit ambiance.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable (in-transit)
meals.lunch: Light snack or premium airport lounge dining before departure
meals.dinner: Beachfront dinner at Phi Phi Don — grilled tiger prawns, red curry with fresh crab, mango sticky rice

day_by_day.notes: Arrange private speedboat transfer in advance. October is shoulder season — expect some rain showers but lush scenery. Check in is typically after 14:00.

day_by_day.morning: Private longtail boat sunrise tour around Phi Phi Leh — visit the iconic Maya Bay (early entry before crowds), snorkel in crystal-clear waters at Pileh Lagoon, and explore hidden sea caves.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a spa treatment — traditional Thai massage or aromatherapy oil massage at the boutique spa. Spend leisure time at the pool or on the beach.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a hilltop viewpoint on Phi Phi Don (Phi Phi Viewpoint trek). Dinner at an upscale Thai restaurant on the island.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — fresh tropical fruit, eggs benedict, Thai congee, freshly squeezed juices
meals.lunch: Light poolside lunch — papaya salad, spring rolls, coconut smoothie bowls
meals.dinner: Fine dining Thai restaurant — massaman lamb curry, steamed sea bass with lime and chili, jasmine rice

day_by_day.notes: Book Maya Bay entry permit in advance as daily visitor numbers are strictly limited. Bring reef-safe sunscreen for snorkeling.

day_by_day.morning: Private island hopping excursion by luxury speedboat — visit Bamboo Island (Koh Mai Phai) for pristine white sand beaches and snorkeling over coral reefs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Mosquito Island (Koh Yung) for more secluded snorkeling. Enjoy a gourmet picnic lunch prepared by the resort served on a private sandbank.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Phi Phi Don. Explore the vibrant street food scene along the main walking street — sample local bites before a sit-down dinner.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — fresh pastries, tropical fruits, Thai omelette with herbs
meals.lunch: Gourmet private picnic on a sandbank — artisan sandwiches, fresh fruit, sparkling water, local snacks
meals.dinner: Street food exploration: pad thai from a top local vendor, grilled satay skewers, mango with sticky rice — followed by cocktails at a beachside bar

day_by_day.notes: Wear water shoes for rocky snorkeling entry points. Bring waterproof bags for electronics on the speedboat.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided kayaking tour through the mangroves and limestone karst formations around Phi Phi Don. Discover hidden lagoons and sea caves accessible only by kayak.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to resort for leisure. Optional: scuba diving certification or discovery dive with a licensed PADI dive center at Phi Phi's renowned dive sites (Shark Point, King Cruiser Wreck).
day_by_day.evening: Beachside fire show and cultural performance at a premium beach club. Enjoy Thai-fusion cuisine and cocktails under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — açaí bowls, smoked salmon bagels, Thai-style fried rice with egg
meals.lunch: Resort restaurant — green curry with chicken, fresh spring rolls, coconut water
meals.dinner: Premium beach club dinner — Thai-fusion tasting menu, signature cocktails, fresh seafood on ice

day_by_day.notes: Book scuba diving in advance as slots fill quickly. The fire show typically starts around 21:00 — confirm timing with resort concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Private speedboat transfer to Krabi mainland. Check in to a luxury resort in Railay Beach or Ao Nang area. Morning at leisure — explore Railay Beach's dramatic limestone cliffs.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rock climbing experience on Railay's world-famous limestone karst walls with a certified guide — suitable for all levels. Alternatively, visit Phra Nang Cave Beach, one of Thailand's most beautiful beaches.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset boat cruise along the Krabi coastline with champagne and canapés. Dinner at a top-rated restaurant in Ao Nang.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — full Thai and Western spread
meals.lunch: Beachside restaurant at Railay — grilled fish with tamarind sauce, som tum, fresh coconut
meals.dinner: Upscale Ao Nang restaurant — tiger prawn tom yum, stir-fried crab with curry powder, jasmine rice

day_by_day.notes: Railay Beach is only accessible by boat — arrange longtail boat transfers. Book rock climbing guide in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Private four-island tour by luxury speedboat from Krabi — visit Koh Poda, Chicken Island (Koh Hua Khwan), Tup Island, and Koh Mor. Snorkel and swim at each stop.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the iconic Tup Island sandbar — a narrow strip of white sand connecting two islands visible only at low tide. Photography session and beach relaxation.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Krabi Town for an authentic street food evening tour with a private guide — explore the night market, sample local delicacies, and visit hidden food stalls.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — fresh fruit platters, eggs to order, Thai-style noodle soup
meals.lunch: Packed gourmet lunch on the boat — fresh sandwiches, tropical fruit, chilled beverages
meals.dinner: Krabi Night Market street food tour — boat noodles, crab fried rice, roti with condensed milk, fresh-pressed sugarcane juice

day_by_day.notes: Check tide times for Tup Island sandbar visibility. Night market is most lively on weekends — confirm days with local guide.

day_by_day.morning: Private longtail boat tour through the Krabi mangroves and sea caves — visit the mysterious Bor Thor caves and observe local wildlife including monitor lizards and tropical birds.
day_by_day.afternoon: Tiger Cave Temple (Wat Tham Suea) visit — climb 1,237 steps to the summit for panoramic views of Krabi's landscape. Visit the sacred cave temple at the base.
day_by_day.evening: Luxury spa evening at the resort — couple's massage, herbal steam bath, and traditional Thai body scrub. Private in-room dinner option.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — smoothie bowls, avocado toast, Thai-style crepes with coconut cream
meals.lunch: Local restaurant near Tiger Cave — khao pad (fried rice), pad see ew, fresh lime soda
meals.dinner: In-room private dining or resort fine dining — set Thai tasting menu with wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Tiger Cave Temple climb is strenuous — wear comfortable shoes and bring water. Start early to avoid midday heat. Dress modestly for temple visit (cover shoulders and knees).

day_by_day.morning: Private luxury transfer to Phuket (approximately 2.5 hours by road or 45 minutes by speedboat). Check in to a 5-star beachfront resort in Surin Beach or Bang Tao area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Surin Beach — one of Phuket's most upscale beaches. Rent a private beach cabana, swim in the Andaman Sea, and enjoy beachside service.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at one of Phuket's renowned fine dining establishments in Cherngtalay or Laguna area — modern Thai cuisine with international influences.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast in Krabi before departure
meals.lunch: Beachside restaurant at Surin — fresh seafood, Thai salads, tropical cocktails
meals.dinner: Award-winning Phuket restaurant — contemporary Thai tasting menu, fresh Andaman seafood, premium wine list

day_by_day.notes: Book Phuket resort well in advance for October. Surin Beach has calmer waters compared to Patong — ideal for a premium experience.

day_by_day.morning: Private guided tour of Old Phuket Town — explore Sino-Portuguese architecture, colorful heritage shophouses, art galleries, and local temples. Visit the iconic Dibuk Road and Thalang Road.
day_by_day.afternoon: Street food deep-dive in Phuket Town with a private culinary guide — taste Phuket-specific dishes like o-tao (oyster omelette), mee hokkien, and khanom jeen (rice noodles with curry).
day_by_day.evening: Sundowner drinks at a rooftop bar overlooking Phuket Town or Patong Bay. Dinner at a premium seafood restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — full buffet with live cooking stations
meals.lunch: Street food tour lunch in Phuket Town — dim sum, Hokkien noodles, local sweets
meals.dinner: Premium seafood restaurant — whole grilled barramundi, steamed clams with Thai herbs, tom kha soup

day_by_day.notes: Phuket Town is a UNESCO candidate site — wear comfortable walking shoes. The street food scene here is distinctly different from other Thai regions due to Chinese-Peranakan influence.

day_by_day.morning: Private yacht charter for a full-day Phang Nga Bay island hopping experience — visit James Bond Island (Koh Tapu), Ko Panyi floating village, and kayak through sea caves and hongs (hidden lagoons).
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the yacht cruise — stop at a secluded bay for swimming and snorkeling. Enjoy a gourmet lunch served on deck with Andaman Sea views.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Phuket. Sunset cocktails on the yacht before docking. Dinner at a beachfront restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast before departure
meals.lunch: Gourmet on-deck lunch — fresh seafood, Thai salads, tropical fruits, chilled wines
meals.dinner: Beachfront fine dining — lobster thermidor Thai-style, grilled whole fish, coconut desserts

day_by_day.notes: Phang Nga Bay yacht charter is a full-day experience — depart by 08:00 for the best experience. Bring seasickness medication if needed.

day_by_day.morning: Elephant sanctuary visit at a reputable ethical sanctuary near Phuket or Khao Lak — feed, bathe, and walk with rescued elephants in a responsible, no-riding environment.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to resort for a relaxing afternoon. Optional: private cooking class at the resort — learn to prepare 4 classic Thai dishes with a master chef.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell beach dinner at a premium beach club — feet in the sand, live acoustic music, fresh seafood BBQ, and signature cocktails.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — fresh juices, Thai congee, eggs to order
meals.lunch: Sanctuary provided lunch or local restaurant — Thai green curry, fresh spring rolls
meals.dinner: Premium beach club BBQ — whole lobster, tiger prawns, grilled fish with lemongrass, sticky rice, tropical desserts

day_by_day.notes: Research and book only ethical elephant sanctuaries that follow no-riding, no-performance policies. This is a highlight experience — book well in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at leisure — last swim in the Andaman Sea, beach walk, or resort spa treatment. Pack and prepare for departure.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private transfer to Phuket International Airport or continue to Bangkok for an optional city extension. If departing, enjoy the airport's premium lounges.
day_by_day.evening: If extending to Bangkok: check in to a luxury hotel on the Chao Phraya River (Mandarin Oriental or similar). Evening river cruise with dinner.

meals.breakfast: Resort breakfast — full spread, champagne optional as a farewell treat
meals.lunch: Airport premium lounge or riverside restaurant in Bangkok
meals.dinner: Bangkok riverside fine dining — royal Thai cuisine, river views, live traditional music

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2.5 hours before international flight for Phuket airport. If extending to Bangkok, book a late checkout at the Phuket resort.

day_by_day.morning: Bangkok exploration (if extended) — private guided tour of the Grand Palace and Wat Phra Kaew (Temple of the Emerald Buddha). Marvel at the gilded architecture and sacred artifacts.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore Bangkok's luxury shopping — visit ICONSIAM or EmQuartier mall. Optional: Wat Pho (Temple of the Reclining Buddha) and traditional Thai massage at the temple's renowned massage school.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Bangkok at a rooftop restaurant with city skyline views — celebrate the end of an extraordinary Thailand journey with a premium Thai feast.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — international and Thai spread with river views
meals.lunch: Upscale Thai restaurant near the Grand Palace — pad thai, tom yum goong, mango sticky rice
meals.dinner: Rooftop fine dining — contemporary Thai cuisine, panoramic Bangkok skyline, premium cocktails and wine

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly for Grand Palace visit (no shorts, sleeveless tops — sarongs available at the entrance). Book rooftop dinner reservation in advance. Arrange airport transfer for departure day.

query: Thailand beaches, $1800 for couple, mix of island hopping and street food, October 2026
